title: Compatibility Certification Matrix for Runtime, API, SDKs, and Console
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Goal: produce a machine-readable compatibility certification matrix and an operational playbook that defines how runtime builds, public API versions, SDK releases, and Console migrations are certified for LTS channels. The end deliverables are: (1) a CSV/JSON matrix mapping runtime ABI/serialization, REST contract, SDK semver compatibility, and Console feature flags; (2) an automated preflight validator that gates canary rollouts; (3) a lightweight migration CLI for customers to preview upgrade impact; and (4) a concise runbook for ops and customer success.

Motivation: engineers and customers have reported upgrade uncertainty across surfaces (e.g., runtime kernel changes that alter KV cache on-disk layout, SDK client header changes causing subtle 400s, and Console dashboard column renames). We need a single source of truth so teams can: plan cohort upgrades, safely pin combinations, and automate rollout gates.

Scope and boundaries: include Redwood serving runtime (inference engine), public REST/streaming API contracts, official SDKs (Python/Node/Go), and Redwood Console. Exclude deep model format compatibility (handled by model-onboarding), and downstream partner integrations (these will be handled via compatibility labels and customer advisories).

Key deliverables: 
- Compatibility matrix (JSON + CSV) documenting: runtime binary version, supported API minor versions, SDK versions that are certified against that runtime/API, Console compatibility notes, known incompatibilities, migration notes, and recommended pin sets.
- Preflight validation scripts (CI job + CLI): schema checks, contract compatibility tests, runtime integration smoke tests, SDK e2e against a pinned public test harness.
- Rollout gate definitions: automated canary cohorts (traffic fractions + percentiles), health signals (5xx spike, token latency P95, cache miss ratio), rollback triggers, and escalation paths.
- Migration CLI: --preview to analyze a customer's current pins and surface required changes and risk.
- Ops playbook: sequence, owner lists, dashboards, post-upgrade validation checklist, and rollback steps.

Success criteria: 
- Matrix published and consumed by release pipelines (CI/CD fails when incompatible combinations are selected).
- At least two internal services and one customer successfully complete a v2.4 LTS upgrade using the playbook with zero customer-facing errors.

Non-goals: automated binary transforms of on-disk formats (out of scope), reworking SDK internals (we may recommend but won’t refactor in this ticket).

References and artifacts: 
- Draft matrix spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/REL/compat-matrix-draft 
- Preflight CI prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-infra/pull/3123 
- Incident notes that motivated this: https://notion.redwood.ai/incident/RW-2024-11-17-kv-compat
- Telemetry dashboard: https://datadog.redwood.ai/dashboards/upgrade-safety
comments: 2025-01-16 - Kickoff: cross-functional meeting with Runtime, API, SDK, Console and Support. Agreement: central matrix + per-surface validators. Action: Runtime to enumerate ABI/serialization invariants by 2025-01-22. (Owner: Liam O'Connor)

2025-01-22 - Runtime update: ABI invariants doc uploaded to the draft spec. We found one compatibility window where cache on-disk index format changes between runtime-2.3 and runtime-2.4; proposed compatibility shim or migration step documented. (Owner: Liam O'Connor)

2025-01-28 - API feedback from PM (Helena Zhou): require explicit deprecation windows for minor API removals, and include contract tests in preflight. Add fields 'deprecation_end' and 'schema_strictness' to matrix rows.

2025-01-30 - SDK leads (Python: Maria Gonzales, Node: Arjun Singh) provided matrix rows for semver guarantees and recommended pinning rules. Noted that Node SDK's streaming deserializer is tolerant; Python is strict. Added compatibility notes. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1429)

2025-02-01 - Design review: Console team requested a 'UI-migration-impact' flag for breaking label changes (column renames, route changes) so Console rollouts can stage feature flags and transformation migrations. (Design owner: Priya Sharma)

2025-02-02 - Risk trade-offs discussion: two options for the runtime on-disk change: (A) implement a one-time migration step at upgrade (higher ops burden, immediate compatibility), (B) ship runtime with compatibility layer for 6 months (more engineering effort, lower ops). Decided to implement (A) for runtime-2.4 LTS and schedule (B) for future long-term strategy. (Decision owner: Ravi Patel)

2025-02-03 - CI integration: initial preflight job runs for internal service 'query-proxy' against runtime-2.4 and checks SDK pins; job fails due to Python SDK pin mismatch. Action: add an automated suggestion in CLI to update pinned SDK version and run local contract test. (CI job: release-infra/preflight/3123)
2025-02-03 - Next steps: finalize matrix schema, wire into release pipeline as a gating artifact, add migration CLI preview mode, schedule customer pilot with partner AcmeAI for Feb 24 - Mar 3.
notes_for_security: KMS usage and migration scripts will be reviewed by security; ensure all migration steps avoid exposing key material and that audit logs are emitted. Contact security lead: Nora Li.
rollback_strategy: Automated canary unwind to previous pinned combo + database read-only mode for affected services; if stateless incompatibility, immediate rollback to previous runtime binary; documented manual steps included in runbook.
telemetry_checks: P95 latency, 5xx rate, token-generation error rate, KV cache miss ratio, SDK deserialization errors. Thresholds: 5xx > 0.1% OR latency P95 increase > 25% triggers rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Matrix JSON published in release-infra repo, preflight CI job added to pipeline, migration CLI prototype with --preview and --apply flags, one internal service validated and one external pilot scheduled.
customer_communication_notes: Prepare advisory emails and console banner for customers in pinned cohorts; include preview tool instructions and fallback steps. Coordinate with success and legal for SLA impact notes.
